# `oaap mail`

the node's mailbox: realms send password resets with it (RFC-0072).

**Root:** needs `sudo`.

## Usage

```sh
oaap mail [--target TARGET] [--from SENDER]
                 [--from-name FROM_NAME] [--reply-to REPLY_TO] [--user USER]
                 [--password-file PASSWORD_FILE] [--yes]
                 {set,show,test,clear} [to]
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `action` | what to do -- see Actions below |
| `to` | for 'test': the address |
| `--target TARGET` | smtps://host:465 (TLS) or smtp://host:587 (STARTTLS, required) |
| `--from SENDER` | the sender address the mail server allows |
| `--from-name FROM_NAME` | the sender's name (a realm uses its tenant's) |
| `--reply-to REPLY_TO` | -- |
| `--user USER` | the login at the server |
| `--password-file PASSWORD_FILE` | a file holding the password (never the command line) |
| `--yes` | for 'clear' |

## Actions

Whether an action needs `sudo` is read from the rule the node enforces, with the other arguments left out (e.g. `node care` reads, `node care measure` needs `sudo`).

| Action | Needs `sudo` |
|---|---|
| `set` | yes |
| `show` | yes |
| `test` | yes |
| `clear` | yes |
